questions.q: Butanoic acid is warmed with HN₃ and concentrated H₂SO₄. The organic product is:
questions.explain: The Schmidt reaction removes the carboxyl carbon as CO₂, so the amine has one carbon fewer than the acid; N₂ is also lost.

questions.q: Which intermediate is common to the Schmidt reaction of a carboxylic acid and the Hofmann bromamide degradation?
questions.explain: Both step-down reactions pass through an isocyanate, which is hydrolysed to a carbamic acid that loses CO₂ to give the amine.

questions.q: Benzophenone is treated with HN₃ in H₂SO₄. The product is:
questions.explain: With a ketone the reagent inserts NH next to the carbonyl by a Beckmann-like shift, giving the amide C₆H₅–CO–NH–C₆H₅.

questions.q: An optically active carboxylic acid R*–COOH undergoes the Schmidt reaction. Which statement about the amine R*–NH₂ is correct?
options: It is racemic because a free carbocation forms
Its configuration is inverted at the migrating carbon
Its configuration is retained at the migrating carbon, showing the shift is intramolecular
It contains the two terminal nitrogens of HN₃
questions.explain: The migrating group moves from C to N with retention. Only the N that carried H in HN₃ ends up in the amine; the other two leave as N₂.
